To answer this question, we need to look at the text in the document "A Sugar-Derived Room-Temperature Sodium Sulfur Battery with Long Term Cycling Stability" (nanolett-6b05172) that describes the results of the rate test and the durability test.

The text states: "At 1C, a capacity >300 mAh/gS is maintained compared to reversible capacities at slow rates of 0.1C where >700 mAh/gS is measured."

The text also states: "With respect to the entire mass of the electrode, the cathode delivers 87 mAh/g after 1500 cycles at 100% depth of discharge (DOD), which is an impressive mass specific performance especially with the moderate loading of 35 wt % active sulfur."

From this, we can conclude that the capacity per gram of sulfur delivered at cycle 1500 at 1C is 87 mAh/g, which is the mass specific performance of the entire electrode.

The text does not provide the information about the share of this capacity of the reversible capacity it showed at 1C in the rate test. However, it states that the cathode delivered a reversible capacity of 370 mAh/gS at high rates of 1C, which is over 50% retention of capacity at 10 times the rate.

We can calculate the share of the capacity at cycle 1500 of the reversible capacity it showed at 1C in the rate test as follows:

(87 mAh/g) / (370 mAh/gS) = 0.235 or 23.5%

So, the capacity per gram of sulfur delivered at cycle 1500 at 1C is 87 mAh/g, which is about 23.5% of the reversible capacity it showed at 1C in the rate test.
